transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-29
Start: 09:30 PST
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan, Avery, Camila, Priya, Samir (QA)
Links shared: preflight checklist (internal doc), perf spreadsheet, kernel fallback runbook (note: links redacted)

Summary:
Quick synchronous preflight for the sprint's beta pressure test. Review of recent kernel fallback incident (last week), discuss amplification of staged traffic, failure modes and fallbacks, and decide short-term guardrails to avoid eviction cascades. Aim to leave with concrete smoke checks and owners.

Topics:
- Beta traffic pacing and ramp script (90/10 plan)
- Kernel fallback postmortem highlights and outstanding risks
- Observability gaps (KV eviction, prefix cache telemetry)
- Rollout gates and oncall staffing for launch weekend

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick agenda, we have 45 ish minutes then we can stay on for questions. main goal is: are we comfortable running the beta pressure test w the new batching/quant profile? what are the guardrails.
[00:18] Avery: yeah, i ran the local sim yesterday, looked promising, but there were a few tails — the kernel fallback path still spikes latency if the sequence length distribution deviates, and the kv cache thrash.. i think i said "kv cash" in the doc, sorry.
[00:32] Camila: yeah the fallback convo — to be clear — last week's incident was an eviction cascade that started after a large prefix flush, something about a migrating run that triggered epoch compaction; the runtime dropped into fallback kernels and then we saw token latencies go to 6x for a slice.
[00:49] Priya: can you restate that, samir had some notes?
[00:53] Samir (QA): i have the timeline — at 14:03 the compactor ran, at 14:04 the kv misses spiked, 14:05 fallback ramped, 14:07 latency alarm. our smoke tests didn't catch this because the prefix distribution in CI is too narrow.
[01:10] Jordan: so the short story is our test matrix didn't cover the long-tail prefix churn, yes.
[01:17] Avery: right, and the quant profile we flip for beta reduces mem but increases sensitivity to fragmentation. that's the tradeoff we discussed — latency vs cost — the usual.
[01:29] Camila: the mitigation we had in prod — reduce concurrent coroutines per model and fallback to the unoptimized path earlier — helped but it added cost and latency. we need something smarter: either a KV backpressure signal or a graceful reject policy.
[01:45] Priya: i think a graceful reject is fine for beta, but we should scope automatic fallback to a compatible variant not too much slower, otherwise customer experience tanks.
[01:55] Jordan: action: add a staged reject policy to the P0 checklist for the beta run. put it on the dashboard.
[02:02] 
[02:10] Avery: on the pressure test: plan is to push 90% normal weight, 10% heavy sessions (long seqs) for 30 minutes, repeat with different quant settings. i want to run against canary pool then escalate.
[02:25] Camila: make sure the canary pool is pinned to a fallback-friendly kernel set — we had mismatched kernels yesterday.
[02:31] Jordan: noted — Avery, can you run the 90/10 script and upload the perf spreadsheet?
[02:36] Avery: yes i'll run it tonight and upload results to the sheet. there's a tiny chance of a cascade but we have rollbacks.
[02:44] Samir: add a step to run prefix-surge patterns — our synthetic generator needs a "compaction-trigger" mode to replicate the compactor timing.
[02:53] 
[03:05] Priya: on observability — we don't have KV eviction rate surfaced in the preflight dashboard. the current metrics show token p95/p99 but don't map to cache health. that made diagnosis slow.
[03:18] Camila: agree, i'll patch the exporter to emit eviction_rate, kv_miss_ratio, and prefix_flush_count. those three should let us correlate. i'll also add an alert when eviction_rate > 0.2 and latency increases.
[03:34] Jordan: put the alert on a separate rollup channel so paging isn't noisy. we only want to page if latency>2s and eviction_rate>0.25 or if p99 error rate spikes.
[03:48] Avery: question — are we comfortable with the quant profile we plan to ship for beta, or do we switch to the safer smaller quantization that keeps more headroom?
[03:56] Priya: safer quant reduces cost savings but increases margin for error. for beta maybe prefer safety. we can flip back post-beta if perf looks good.
[04:07] Jordan: consensus — use the safer quant for initial beta run. update the rollout matrix.
[04:13] 
[04:20] Samir: QA will extend smoke tests: add long-seq generator, compaction-trigger mode, and a ramp that simulates KV thrash. i'll need a dev cluster with the same kernel set.
[04:33] Camila: i'll provision a small dev cluster and pin the kernels, then share creds. note: it's ephemeral but ok for QA.
[04:40] 
[04:46] Priya: staffing — who covers on-call during the test window and launch weekend? we need an escalation path if fallback occurs.
[04:52] Jordan: Priya and Camila own on-call scheduling. Priya, you get point for launch weekend, Camila is backup for runtime issues, Avery for rollout/SE, and Samir for QA validation.
[05:05] Priya: i'll publish rota by feb 5th. also, let's do a dry-run alert drill before the beta ramp so everyone knows who pages.
[05:15] Jordan: yes, plan a 30 minute drill mid next week.
[05:20] 
[05:28] Avery: one more thing — we should add a canary fallback variant that's quant-safer but same model arch. the runtime can route to it if cache pressure detected. that's lower risk than full fallback to unoptimized kernel.
[05:40] Camila: that's good; but we need a fast signal. i'll prototype a probe: a small N token probe that verifies KV hits before routing. if probe fails, route to safer quant variant.
[05:53] Jordan: put that probe as a P1 in the backlog but P0 for launch if it's quick to implement.
[05:59] 
[06:05] Samir: test coverage note: our integration harness assumes uniform prompt lengths; we should randomize lengths and prefixes to better exercise cache behaviors.
[06:17] Avery: agreed — i'll update harness and push patch.
[06:22] 
[06:30] Priya: any blockers on release gating? known ones: missing kv metrics on dashboard, missing long-seq smoke tests, no canary fallback variant yet. those are manageable within two weeks if owners act.
[06:45] Jordan: ok let's recap decisions: 1) safer quant for beta 2) run 90/10 ramp against pinned canary pool 3) add eviction metrics and alerts 4) add staged reject policy & canary fallback variant as tactical fallbacks 5) dry-run alert drill next week 6) owners for oncall published.
[07:05] Camila: i'll open the ticket for eviction metrics and post PR by EOD tomorrow.
[07:11] Avery: i'll run the pressure test tonight and post results; then run again after metric changes.
[07:18] Samir: QA will extend smoke tests and send the new harness to the sheet.
[07:24] Priya: i'll coordinate rota and publish the launch weekend plan.
[07:30] Jordan: great, thanks all. any other concerns?
[07:35] (brief pause)
[07:38] Camila: one late concern — third party kernel patch scheduled next week by Ops, we should ensure it's not applied to canary during tests.
[07:46] Jordan: good catch — Ops, hold patch on canary until we confirm. Priya will confirm with ops.
[07:52] Jordan: meeting adjourned, i'll follow up the checklist and post notes.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Avery: run 90/10 canary pressure test; upload perf sheet (due 2026-02-02)
- Camila: add eviction metrics + alert + pin kernel set to canary (due 2026-02-03)
- Priya: publish oncall rota and confirm ops patch hold (due 2026-02-05)
- Samir: extend QA harness and add compaction-trigger mode (due 2026-02-04)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels were corrected where obvious; some technical terms transcribed phonetically ("kv cash" means KV cache). references to internal docs were represented as notes rather than full URLs.
